Methods: Verify inverse functions using both composition identities, each on its applicable domain; unrestricted squaring followed by the principal square root returns the absolute value. Find inverse rules by interchanging x and y and making y the subject. Reflection in y=x interchanges coordinates, intercepts and horizontal/vertical features. The domain and range interchange under inversion. Use an appropriate one-to-one domain restriction and select the inverse branch consistent with its range. A function is one-to-one when every horizontal line intersects its graph at most once; equal outputs then imply equal inputs. For increasing functions, inverse intersections lie on y=x and can be found from f(x)=x with domain checks. Decreasing functions may also have off-diagonal intersections; the taught example f(x)=-x^3 intersects its inverse at (-1,1), (0,0) and (1,-1).
